king.name: King of Eolis
lines: Wanderer. You return to a dying town.
The springs that fed the World Tree have stopped. Our fountain is dust, and the dwarves who share the roots with us have turned savage.
Something fell from the sky and took root in the Tree. I fear it drinks the springs.
Take this purse: 1,500 gold. Arm yourself well, then go down into the Trunk Hollows and find out why the Spring of Trunk is silent.
lines_after: The Trunk Hollows lie past the east gate. Rest at the Guru first.
If the spring flows again, Eolis will know. The fountain will tell us.

guru.name: Guru
guru.greeting: Breathe, wanderer. Rest here, or let me teach your body what your mind already knows.

townsfolk_well.name: Old Wena
lines: Forty years I drew water from that fountain. Now I draw dust.
My grandson went into the roots to look for the spring. He said the sap was moving. Sap doesn't move.

townsfolk_well_glad.name: Old Wena
lines: Full! Forty years, and I never saw it brim like this. Listen to it.
My grandson came home this morning, soaked to the skin and laughing. He says the rain up top has stopped.

festival_piper.name: Festival Piper
lines: Eolis hasn't danced since the meteor fell. Three springs running, three days of music, the Elder says.
They say the dwarves of Dartmoor still sleep under the water. Somebody ought to wake them. Not me, mind. I pipe.

townsfolk_gate.name: Gate Watch
lines: East gate leads down into the Trunk Hollows. Monodrons hop about near the entrance. Watch the eye: it flashes before it jumps.
The rot dwarves carry shields. Get behind them, or wait for the swing and hit back.

apolune_widow.name: Hesk
lines: Apolune, they called it. The town in the hollow. Now it's me and the Guru and the drip of the sap.
When the spring went quiet the sap started to crawl. It filled the lanes in a night. The others ran for Eolis.
If you mean to go deeper, the shrine below keeps you safe. Past it, a shaft climbs east to the dwarves' old hall.

apolune_widow_glad.name: Hesk
lines: The sap went hard as glass in an hour. You did that, didn't you?
Brannoc and Tilde came back the next morning. Shops open, lamps lit. It almost feels like a town.

apolune_miner.name: Dwarf Orrin
lines: Not every dwarf turned. Those of us who kept away from the meteor's light kept our heads.
The Tower of Trunk is ours, or was. Zoradohna holds it now. Bring a Mattock if you go: the old walls only crack for one.

dartmoor_steward.name: Steward Hrafna
lines: The water is going down. I can hear it in the stair, running away below, for the first time since the king made his bargain.
He let the meteor into him so his people would live. It kept us, after a fashion: asleep under the flood. You have given him his rest, and us our waking.
His ring is yours. The gate of Zenis is up the Meteor Rise, east of here. And below us, under the last stone, the Sunken Spring still holds its water. Let it lie, for now.

dartmoor_mason.name: Mason Brokk
lines: Woke on my back in the market with weed in my beard. The tide line's a foot lower already.
We'll have the lower city dry by spring. Mind the water-clocks, though: they still hold their hour.

forepaw_elder.name: Elder Basalt
lines: You freed him. Dunmar, our champion. He climbed into that engine to hold the meteor's men back, and the crystal took him instead.
The meteor fell into the Tree's crown years ago. Our king, Grieve, went up to bargain with what lives inside it.
He has not come back as himself. Take the Ruby Ring, elf. It was forged in Forepaw, and the gate of Zenis will know it.

forepaw_miner.name: Dwarf Tamsin
lines: Three years we hid in the deep galleries while that drill chewed the halls.
The lift runs again. Ride it down to the Tower Foot and you'll be back in the Trunk in a breath.

forepaw_digger.name: Dwarf Okko
lines: Hrothgar's forge is lit! Bring him your blade. He'll fold it twice if your purse is heavy enough.
Up the trunk the mist begins. Nobody who went into it came back dry.

conflate_elder.name: Elder Aelwen
lines: An elf of Eolis, climbing the Tree from the roots? Then the springs below run again. We felt the sap stir.
Above us, on the crown-leaf, a flower took root the year the meteor fell. We call it Pakukame, the Devouring Bloom. It eats the light, and those who go to look at it.
Our wardens crossed the sky-gaps with the Elven Stride. Its shrine is in the Windloft, up the north bough. If you mean to face the Bloom, go there first.

conflate_warden.name: Warden Faelan
lines: Hold. You came over the bridge? Past the mantises? Then keep your blade out, elf. You've earned it.
The north bough climbs to the crown-leaf. Nobody goes up there now. The last warden who tried, the Bloom swallowed whole.

conflate_weaver.name: Weaver Imra
lines: Leaf-silk, spun in the sun. It won't stop a blade, but it keeps the wind off.
The dwarves used to climb up to trade iron for silk. Then the meteor came, and the dwarves stopped climbing, and some stopped being dwarves.

daybreak_mayor.name: Mayor Halloran
lines: You crossed the fallen bridge? Then the Bloom is dead, and the wind brought us a hero. Welcome to Daybreak.
Our bells and lifts ran on the storm. Lightning came down the rods and the copper sang. Then a great bird came out of the clouds and the conduits went cold.
Borabohra, we call it. It nests in the Spires above the town. Nothing that flies is safe, and nothing that climbs.

daybreak_bellkeeper.name: Old Bellkeeper Rusk
lines: The old bell cellar? Bramble choked it the year the storm turned. Blades only snag in that stuff.
Ysolde sells a scroll of Fire. Dry bramble goes up like tinder. I'd do it myself, but I'm too old to aim.
